record.paper_title: Open problems originated in our research work with Zoltán Daróczy
record.original_question: Fix a non-integer q > 1, write θ = 1/q and k = [q], and let A_k = {0,1,…,k}. A function F:[0,1)→ℂ is additive with respect to the Rényi–Parry expansion if F(0)=0, ∑_{l≥1}∑_{a=1}^k |F(aθ^l)| < ∞, and for each x\in[0,1) one has F(x)=∑_{n≥1} F(ε_n(x)θ^n), where ε_n(x) are the digits of the regular expansion of x. Let t=t_1t_2⋯ be the quasi-regular expansion of 1, let G(z)=1-t_1z-t_2z^2-⋯, and call a continuous additive function elementary if it belongs to the closed linear span of the functions generated by sequences u_ν=ν^jρ^ν, where ρ is a root of G(z)=0 in |z|<1 and 0\le j<m-1 when m is the multiplicity of ρ. Is every continuous additive function elementary?

evidence.quote: Theorem 1. If F : I1 → C is a continuous additive function, then F (jθ n) = jF (θn) ( j ∈ A k, n ∈ N).
Such types of continuous additive functions, and even the elements of the closed space generated by such functions called to be elementary continuous additive functions, also.
We formulated our conjecture that every continuous additive function is elementary.

artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not locate a published resolution of this specific conjecture that every continuous additive function with respect to the Rényi–Parry $q$-expansion is elementary. Related work on greedy/quasi-greedy expansions and on Daróczy–Kátai conjectures exists, but no source directly confirms or refutes this statement.

status_evidence.title: Greedy and quasi-greedy expansions in non-integer bases
status_evidence.snippet: Extends results of Rényi, Parry, Daróczy and Kátai concerning expansions in non-integer bases.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on Rényi-Parry expansions exists but does not address the elementary-additive conjecture directly.
